## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

# OMG (Oh My GitHub) agent instructions

Do not implement, suggest, report, or propose security issues unless the user explicitly asks for a security review.
Inspect the OpenCode implementation at `/Users/igor/Documents/ChatGPT/opencode` and [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) for related requests.

## Wiki index

- [OpenCode workflow](wiki/opencode.md)
- [Test OpenCode execution](wiki/opencode-v2-experiment.md)
- [Oh My Github App](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/oh-my-github-app.md)
- [Temporary Mac SSH access](wiki/access.md)
- [Testing and verification](wiki/testing.md)
- [OmGithub publishing](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/omgithub.md)


## Main project file

The main project file is [.github/workflows/opencode.yml](.github/workflows/opencode.yml).

Keep the local [game issue E2E skill](.agents/skills/game-issue-e2e/SKILL.md)
aligned with this workflow. Create an issue with `OpenCode` and only user-requested mode labels already attached, to start the native `issues.opened` listener. Wait only for the
initial OpenCode session link during E2E kickoff. Install the listener on the
default branch before requesting execution. Validate author access and freeze
the request inside Actions before starting the reusable execution job.
Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author
for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup
helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue.
Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the
project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation
dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run.

## Shell timing

When writing shell scripts,
always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands.
Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command;
the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is
slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in
interactive shell commands.

## Ideas

Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under
`./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as
`ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`.




## Links in handoffs

When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown
link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull
requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather
than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use
the `codex://threads/<thread-id>` URL format.

When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days.

function makePath(root, points, width, material) {
  const curve = new THREE.CatmullRomCurve3(points.map(p => new THREE.Vector3(p[0], 0, p[1])))
  const steps = 90
  const positions = []
  const colors = []
  const base = new THREE.Color('#b08a5c')
  const left = []
  const right = []
  const sampleColors = []
  for (let i = 0; i <= steps; i++) {
    const t = i / steps
    const p = curve.getPoint(t)
    const tangent = curve.getTangent(t)
    const nx = -tangent.z
    const nz = tangent.x
    const len = Math.hypot(nx, nz) || 1
    const half = width * (0.85 + 0.3 * Math.sin(t * 9.1))
    const lx = p.x + (nx / len) * half
    const lz = p.z + (nz / len) * half
    const rx = p.x - (nx / len) * half
    const rz = p.z - (nz / len) * half
    left.push(new THREE.Vector3(lx, heightAt(lx, lz) + 0.09, lz))
    right.push(new THREE.Vector3(rx, heightAt(rx, rz) + 0.09, rz))
    sampleColors.push(base.clone().offsetHSL(0, 0, (Math.sin(t * 13.7) + Math.sin(t * 5.3)) * 0.02))
  }
  const pushColor = (c) => colors.push(c.r, c.g, c.b)
  for (let i = 0; i < steps; i++) {
    const l0 = left[i]
    const r0 = right[i]

    ctx.lineWidth = 1.6 + rand() * 1.4

    ctx.moveTo(x, size)
    ctx.quadraticCurveTo(x, size - h * 0.55, x + (rand() - 0.5) * 14, size - h)

}

function makeGrass(root, rng, blocked) {
  const texture = makeGrassBladeTexture()
  const geo = new THREE.PlaneGeometry(1, 1, 1, 1)
  geo.translate(0, 0.5, 0)
  const geoCross = geo.clone()
  geoCross.rotateY(Math.PI / 2)

  const mat = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({
    map: texture,
    alphaTest: 0.32,
    transparent: false,
    side: THREE.DoubleSide,
    roughness: 1,
    metalness: 0,
  })
  const palette = ['#78c24f', '#8ad263', '#67b344', '#97d975', '#5fa73f'].map(c => new THREE.Color(c))
  const count = 4200
  const meshA = new THREE.InstancedMesh(geo, mat, count)
  const meshB = new THREE.InstancedMesh(geoCross, mat, count)
  meshA.receiveShadow = true
  meshB.receiveShadow = true
  const dummy = new THREE.Object3D()
  let placed = 0
  let guard = 0
  while (placed < count && guard++ < count * 10) {
    let x
    let z
    if (rng() < 0.68) {
      const angle = rng() * Math.PI * 2
      const radius = Math.sqrt(rng()) * 52
      x = 10 + Math.cos(angle) * radius
      z = 30 + Math.sin(angle) * radius
    } else {
      x = (rng() - 0.5) * 150
      z = (rng() - 0.5) * 150
    }
    const h = heightAt(x, z)
    if (h < 0.85 || h > 14) continue
    if (slopeAt(x, z) > 0.4) continue
    if (blocked(x, z, 1.3)) continue
    const w = 0.7 + rng() * 0.75
    const height = 0.55 + rng() * 0.65
    dummy.position.set(x, h - 0.04, z)
    dummy.rotation.set(0, rng() * Math.PI * 2, 0)
    dummy.scale.set(w, height, w)
    dummy.updateMatrix()
    meshA.setMatrixAt(placed, dummy.matrix)
    meshB.setMatrixAt(placed, dummy.matrix)
    const color = palette[Math.floor(rng() * palette.length)]
    meshA.setColorAt(placed, color)
    meshB.setColorAt(placed, color)
    placed++
  }
  meshA.count = meshB.count = placed
  meshA.instanceMatrix.needsUpdate = true
  meshB.instanceMatrix.needsUpdate = true
  if (meshA.instanceColor) meshA.instanceColor.needsUpdate = true
  if (meshB.instanceColor) meshB.instanceColor.needsUpdate = true
  root.add(meshA, meshB)
}

let roofTileTex = null
function roofTileTexture() {
  if (roofTileTex) return roofTileTex
  const c = document.createElement('canvas')
  c.width = c.height = 256
  const ctx = c.getContext('2d')
  ctx.fillStyle = '#f7f2ea'
  ctx.fillRect(0, 0, 256, 256)
  const rows = 9
  const rowH = 256 / rows
  for (let r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
    const y = r * rowH
    ctx.fillStyle = r % 2 === 0 ? 'rgba(255,255,255,0.10)' : 'rgba(70,40,25,0.07)'
    ctx.fillRect(0, y, 256, rowH)
    ctx.strokeStyle = 'rgba(55,30,20,0.22)'
    ctx.lineWidth = 3
    ctx.beginPath()
    ctx.moveTo(0, y + rowH)
    ctx.lineTo(256, y + rowH)
    ctx.stroke()
    const cols = 9
    for (let k = 0; k <= cols; k++) {
      const x = (k / cols) * 256 + (r % 2 ? 14 : 0)
      ctx.strokeStyle = 'rgba(55,30,20,0.13)'
      ctx.lineWidth = 2
      ctx.beginPath()
      ctx.moveTo(x, y)
      ctx.lineTo(x, y + rowH)
      ctx.stroke()
    }
  }
  for (let i = 0; i < 500; i++) {
    ctx.fillStyle = `rgba(${70 + Math.random() * 40},${45 + Math.random() * 30},${30 + Math.random() * 20},${Math.random() * 0.09})`
    ctx.fillRect(Math.random() * 256, Math.random() * 256, 2, 2)
  }
  const tex = new THREE.CanvasTexture(c)
  tex.wrapS = tex.wrapT = THREE.RepeatWrapping
  tex.repeat.set(3, 2)
  tex.colorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace
  tex.anisotropy = 4
  roofTileTex = tex
  return tex
}

Image read successfully

Better composition, sun visible (big white orb top center-left), sky blue, clouds. Path is light tan now and readable though it looks like a "tongue" ending at bottom center under avatar; the path starts at spawn but only visible ahead? It ends abruptly at the bottom edge (spawn) because path start (8,46) is just behind avatar at z=46; camera at z=57 sees path from z=46 forward, and the start edge is a rounded cut behind the avatar. It looks like a beige patch with a curved end at the avatar's feet. Add a stone spawn pad or extend path back to camera bottom (e.g., start z=60) so it runs off-screen, and add path width consistency. Let's extend the main path start to (6,60) → behind camera, so path flows in from bottom. Add points [[7,58],[8,50],[10,40]...]. Then it will run under the camera and look natural.

But path blocked grass along it; good. Also spawn at (8,45) on it.

2. House now has textured roof (visible tile lines), looks better. But the house is still large right and its wall/roof are cut at the top edge? The roof top goes off screen top-right? It's cut by frame. That's okay; framing.

3. Grass still dark, spiky; but acceptable. The foreground is still dominated by blades. Could reduce grass density near the camera and make patches. Alternatively use a shorter/wider look and richer color. The blades appear dark because they're mostly unlit? Their normals face sideways, sun ahead → backlit? They are dark green with bright tips. Hmm.

Could add a second "clover" ground cover? Maybe unnecessary.

4. Trees: canopies dark green, still a bit flat. But with sun low they're backlit; fill light helps. Could lighten palette more (#6cbf55 etc. already). Maybe increase hemi ground color brightness. Or reduce flatShading harshness. Let's brighten leaf palette further and add emissive? Don't.

5. Sun is huge white blob without a defined disc (looks like a full moon). Our sun sprite is a radial gradient at 78 scale; the shader disc is small. It appears as a white circle ~90px with soft edge — acceptable stylized sun, but too white and no rays. Could tint the sprite warmer (gold) and smaller (60) to look like a sun; add a larger faint glow. Currently sprite material's map is white-yellow; tone mapping makes white. Reduce opacity to 0.9 and make texture warmer (#ffdf9e). Also the sun appears above/left; fine.

6. Water now: light teal band with white foam edge visible; looks better. But it's mostly hidden by the bank due to camera angle. Bridge crossing visible. Fine.

7. Bridge: appears as a thin brown line with lanterns; good.

8. Path at bridge is visible as a tan strip leading. Good.

9. The distant left house (blue) is hidden behind trees; fine. Windmill not visible (far left, maybe out of frame / behind trees). Hilltop house visible right distance.

10. Clouds: a bit too many and too flat, but charming. The cloud right above house overlaps roof? fine.

11. Avatar shadow: long and dark to the left? Visible as a dark band under/left of avatar, okay.

12. The sign: now visible right of avatar with text "LUSH VALLEY" (the BRIDGE arrow hidden by coin glow). The sign has a big yellow coin glow overlapping; coin at (12,37) is between sign and avatar. It's a glowing ball; still not coin-like. We can make coins less glow and larger body. Maybe add a vertical "floating coin" emblem: since coins spin around Y, they sometimes show face; at this instant coin shows as a ring? The yellow blob could be the coin itself with glow. At 20 units away, a 1-unit coin appears 20px, but blob is ~60px. So glow dominates. Reduce glow scale to 1.4, opacity 0.25; increase coin radius 0.55 and maybe make the coin emissive brighter so body visible. Do it.

12b. Coins at distance on bridge are orange glows; with smaller glow, body visible.

13. Terrain: bright green; okay. A bit uniformly green; but path, flowers, grass help.

14. The sky/hills transition: pale haze band, fine.

15. HUD hint is now one line; good. Toast not shown.

16. Title screen needs a new screenshot after redesign; check later.

Now gameplay testing: movement, jumping, coin collection, mobile. Also test during title: orbit. Need to verify no runtime errors and controls work.

Functional checks via playwright:
- press W for 2s, screenshot → avatar moves forward along path.
- press Space, check y changes.
- collect coin: teleport player? We can eval in page? Player not exposed globally. Could expose `window.__valley` for debugging (not ideal but okay). Add `window.__valley = { player, props, ... }` in main for testing; harmless. Then simulate collecting by moving player near coin: set player.position to coin pos and wait, check HUD. Better test by keyboard only? We can expose.

But first visual: more polish.

Path extension: change path start to (7,60) through (8,50) to (10,40) etc. The spawn is at (8,45). Blocked grass along path; good.

Coin near path at (12,37) is 2.5 from path center (9,34)? At z=37 path ~x=9.5, coin x=12, 2.5 away — just outside grass path blocking 2.25; fine, coin sits on grass edge. Good.

House branch path from (8,33) to (21,37) passes near coin? fine.

Grass color: perhaps tint blades more yellow-green to match terrain: hsl hue 90-105. Current 96-118 (greener). The terrain is yellow-green (#5aa43e → hue ~100). Fine.

Maybe use smaller count/height near camera. The camera is at ground+3.9; blades 0.6 max. Looks fine.

The main thing making the meadow look "spiky" is the blade texture's sharp tips and the high density with dark color. Real Roblox grass is smooth terrain; perhaps remove most grass blades and rely on terrain texture + flowers. But then meadow looks plain. A middle ground: reduce grass count to 2600, height 0.35, use wider blades (texture width 4-7) → softer. And make material color lighter. Let's do: count 2800, height 0.25-0.5, tall 0.65, texture light 60-72, width 3-5.5, palette near-white. Should look like a lawn with tufts.

Also add small wildflower patches (done).

Sun: make texture warmer and smaller.

Coins: reduce glow.

Add ambient birds? Later.

Add pines? Let's evaluate composition: distant hills need more variety; currently round trees. Pines would add. I'll add a small pine function (maybe 40) on upper slopes to improve horizon.

Let's implement:
- path extension

Composition: house right, sign right, bridge left, sun. It's decent but lacks lushness. The task is "lush valley" — needs denser, rich vegetation. Options:

The coin near sign still shows as a glowing orange ball (at ~688,410). Hmm coin body is probably edge-on and glow sprite; too round. Maybe replace coin visuals with a blocky star/coin that's always face-on to camera (billboard sprite of a coin)? Roblox coins spin, but for readability, use a coin mesh plus a golden star sprite that faces camera. Or make coin geometry a torus with a glowing core that reads as a ring. The blob is because additive glow at 1.5 scale ~30px, coin maybe 15px edge. Let's make coins billboard sprites with a drawn coin texture and a subtle 3D torus; or keep 3D but no additive glow; add a point of light? Simpler: create a sprite with a canvas-drawn coin (gold circle with star) that always faces camera, plus a small glow halo. Then coins look like coins from any angle, Roblox-ish. Add a subtle spin by rotating sprite material.rotation over time? Sprites can rotate in screen space (material.rotation) which looks like spinning coin! Great: sprite coin texture, glow behind, rotation animated. 2D billboard coin with slight 3D rim? Could just use the sprite and skip mesh, but shadows/3D feel lost. Use both: 3D mesh spinning edge visible plus sprite? confusing.

Alternative: use a billboard coin sprite only (with glow), rotated around screen z slowly? A spinning 2D coin (squash horizontally via scale.x = |cos|) gives a convincing spin. Sprite scale.x oscillates. This is easy and looks like a spinning coin always readable. Do:
- canvas coin texture: gold circle with rim, star, shine.
- Sprite material transparent, rotation? We can scale sprite.scale.x = 0.9*abs(cos(t)) + 0.1? Sprite scale in world units; set x scale based on cos to simulate spin, keep y constant. That mimics rotation but front/back identical.
- Add glow sprite behind.
- Keep a small 3D torus? Not needed.
- Collection unaffected.
- Coin casts no shadow (sprite) — fine; glow adds.

Rename coin group; update props.update spin: coin.sprite.scale.x = ... using phase. Need access. We can keep coin mesh but hide? Simpler: replace mesh+rim+star with sprite. Let's implement sprite-based coins and animate squash.

Coin canvas 256: draw circle gradient gold, dark rim, star center, highlight. Set position at ground+1.55, scale 1.3. Spin: scale.x = max(0.12, abs(cos(time*2 + phase))) * 1.3; maybe add slight y bob. Glow sprite scale 2 at opacity .3 behind. Trees at the sides: left near (-20,50), right (35,45). They'd frame the shot. Current clear radius 17 around spawn; add hero trees at (-16,52) and (34,48) with big scale → frame left/right. But house is at right (20,36); tree at (34,48) far right. Left tree at (-16,52) could show at left edge. Good. Terrain texture: currently smooth flat green with faint noise; add visible detailed grass texture by increasing texture repeat? Let's inspect: the flat areas look almost solid green with slight mottling. The texture repeat 86 over 420 → 4.9 units per tile. At 10 units away, the texture should show big roughness. messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a Roblox-style 3D browser game inspired by the user's garbled request "Make huss vally in robl9x", interpreted as "Lush Valley" (Roblox Studio is unavailable in this environment).

## Requirements
- User gave no additional constraints beyond the garbled request; the clarifying question was auto-cancelled because this is a non-interactive run.
- Must be a playable browser game with Roblox-like blocky avatar and lush valley theme.
- Support desktop and mobile touch controls.

## Decisions
- Interpreted "huss vally" as "Lush Valley"; built it with Three.js + Vite instead of Roblox Studio.
- Third-person blocky "Explorer" avatar, river, wooden bridge, cottages, windmill, campfire, 12 collectible coins, path, flowers, grass, trees/pines.
- Added HUD, title screen, completion overlay, procedural WebAudio, mobile joystick/jump button.
- Exposed `window.__valley` debug hook for testing.

## Work State
### Completed
- Vite + Three.js project set up; builds successfully (`npm run build`).
- Terrain heightfield, vertex-colored grass, grass detail texture, animated water shader, shoreline foam, sky shader, sun sprite, clouds, fog, lighting.
- Props: 3 cottages with textured roofs/windows/porches, fences, sign, bridge, windmill, campfire, rocks, bushes, flowers, reeds, pines, 220 trees.
- Player avatar with face texture, name tag, walk animation, third-person camera.
- Movement/jump/sprint, water blocking, house colliders, bridge walkable surface, coin collection, sparkles, pollen.
- Sprite-based spinning coins (improved readability).
- Desktop HUD/title/completion UI and mobile controls; audio kit.
- Server started in tmux on port 3002 (`/tmp/opencode/valley.log`), Playwright works after installing `chromium-1243`.
- Screenshots iterated through `screenshots/game1.png` … `game8.png`; latest `game8.png` shows sun/sky, coin sprites, textured path, visible house/bridge.

### Active
- Final visual polish pass after latest edits (denser grass distributing 9000 clumps near spawn, path dirt texture with UVs, sun sprite now normal-blended warm, sky disc reduced) — edits applied but **not yet rebuilt/screenshotted/verified**.
- Need to verify no runtime errors after these last edits.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Wait for Vite watch rebuild; reload `http://localhost:3002`, click `#play`, take new screenshot (e.g. `screenshots/game9.png`) and inspect.
2. Check console log for shader/runtime errors, especially water/foam/sky path changes.
3. Verify gameplay: W/A/S/D movement, Shift sprint, Space jump, drag look; use `window.__valley` to test coin collection/HUD and completion overlay.
4. Test title screen appearance and mobile viewport/touch layout.
5. Fix any visual issues (grass density/color, path flatness, sun/coin appearance, house framing).
6. Run production capture via `CAPTURE_URL`/`CAPTURE_DIR` if desired and confirm no HTTP/console errors.
7. Update README if appropriate; leave changes uncommitted unless requested.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js`: scene, renderer, lights, loop, UI wiring, sparkles/pollen, coin collection, debug hook.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/props.js`: all props, sky/clouds/sun, grass, flowers, path, houses, bridge, pines, coins.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/terrain.js`: height function, terrain mesh/colors, water shader, foam.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/player.js`: avatar build, input, physics, camera.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/audio.js`: procedural ambient/chime/jump audio.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/styles.css`: title, HUD, mobile controls styling.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: UI markup and entry script.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/start.sh`: serves built app on port 3002 via runtime default-start.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/package.json`: Vite/Three deps and scripts.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/screenshots/game8.png`: latest verified gameplay screenshot.
- `/tmp/opencode/valley.log`: server/build log (tmux session `valley`).

## Important Context
- Playwright browser mismatch was fixed by running `playwright-cli install-browser chromium` (now `chromium-1243` installed).
- Xvfb display file contains `0`; `playwright-cli` wrapper handles `DISPLAY=:0`.
- Use `playwright-cli click "#play"` (the Play button's accessible name is "Play Lush Valley", so clicking by text "Play" fails).
- Server auto-rebuilds on file change via Vite watch; allow ~5–6s before reloading.
- Latest applied but unverified edits: grass `count = 9000` with new near-spawn distribution; `makeDirtTexture()` plus path UVs (`v = t * 22`); sun sprite changed to `NormalBlending` opacity 0.92; sky disc factor 0.9.
- Mobile controls appear only with `body.touch` (coarse pointer/touch detection).
- Current gameplay spawn is `(8, 45)`; camera pitch `0.05`, distance `12.5`; sun direction `(-0.22, 0.3, -0.93)`.
- Do not claim GPU acceleration; environment uses SwiftShader/CPU rendering.

A small Roblox-style 3D playground built with Three.js. Wander a sunlit valley, cross the old
wooden bridge, and collect all twelve gold coins.

sprint, `Space` to jump, and drag the mouse to look around. On a phone or tablet, use the
on-screen joystick and **Jump** button.

bundle in `dist/`.
